title: game-gz-bootstrap uses stale log path and misreports failures
description:
Deep analysis of `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g1/` exposed two correctness bugs in `scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py`, the helper used at the start of deep-analysis runs.

Running `uv run python scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py game_20260309_012143_g1` reported `LLM events: 337 | Failed tool calls: 11` even though the export for that same game shows both players at `toolCallsFailed: 0` and the raw pilot / MCP / error logs are clean. The first reported "failure" is a normal `get_action_choices` response that contains `"required":true`; the script currently treats any serialized tool result containing `error`, `out of range`, `required`, or `failed` as a failed tool call, so mandatory prompts are counted as errors.

The same script also still points its raw-log fallback at `~/mage-bench-logs`, but logs now live under `~/.mage-bench/logs`. If an export is missing, `game-gz-bootstrap.py` therefore reports that raw logs are missing and never runs `scripts/export_game.py`, even when the game exists locally.

Evidence:
- `uv run python scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py game_20260309_012143_g1` printed `Failed tool calls: 11` for a game whose runtime logs had no errors.
- `website/public/games/game_20260309_012143_g1.json` reports `toolCallsFailed: 0` for both `Opus Brewer` and `GPT53C Teach`.
- `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g1/errors.log` contains only `No errors detected.` and both `*_mcp.log` files have no bridge-side error signatures.
- `scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py:18` uses `Path.home() / "mage-bench-logs"` instead of `~/.mage-bench/logs`.
- `scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py:64-72` substring-matches `required` inside tool results and counts those rows as failed calls.
- `git log --oneline --since="2026-03-09" origin/master -- scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py` was empty during investigation, so this does not appear to have been fixed yet.

Source: `scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py:18` and `scripts/game-gz-bootstrap.py:64-72`.

Suggested fix: point the script at the shared `~/.mage-bench/logs` location (or reuse the canonical log-dir helper) and parse tool results structurally before counting failures. Only explicit error indicators such as `success:false`, known bridge error keys, or actual MCP error payloads should increment the failure count.
